note.explanation: Viruses are acellular particles at the borderline of living and non-living. They contain DNA or RNA inside a protein coat, cannot carry out metabolism, and need a host organism to make proteins and increase in number. They are not placed in the classification system because they lack the characteristics of the three domains of life. Prions consist only of protein, while viroids consist only of circular RNA.
examples: A bacteriophage is a virus that attacks bacteria.
An influenza virus is another example of a virus.
note.checkAnswer: They are acellular and lack the characteristics of the three domains of life.
note.simple: A virus is not made of cells and cannot do everything a living organism does by itself. It must use a host to make more viruses, so it does not fit into the three-domain classification of life.
note.checkQuestion: Why are viruses not included in the classification system?
note.title: Viruses and classification
steps: Check whether the particle is made of cells: viruses are acellular.
Check whether it can carry out metabolism: viruses cannot run metabolism.
Remember that viruses use a host to make proteins and increase in number.
Conclude that viruses lack the characteristics of the three domains of life, so they are not included in the classification system.
note.answer: Viruses are acellular and lack the characteristics of the three domains of life, so they are not included in the classification system.

explain.title: Viruses are acellular
explain.body: Viruses are ultramicroscopic creatures that are at the borderline of living and non-living. They are acellular i.e., they are not made of cells and do not have organelles.

explain.title: What a virus contains
explain.body: A virus consists of nucleic acid (DNA or RNA) surrounded by a protein coat. A virus contains either DNA or RNA.

explain.title: Viruses depend on a host
explain.body: They cannot run metabolism. For the synthesis of their proteins and to increase in number, viruses become parasites in organisms (plants, animals, and bacteria).

explain.title: Why viruses are not classified
explain.body: Viruses are not included in the classification system because they lack any of the characteristics of the three domains of life. Prions and viroids are also acellular particles and are also not included in the classification system. Prions are composed of protein only and Viroids are composed of circular RNA only.

mistakes: Do not say that viruses are cells or have organelles; they are acellular.
Do not say viruses contain both DNA and RNA; a virus consists of DNA or RNA.
Do not confuse prions and viroids: prions are protein only, while viroids are circular RNA only.
Do not give only the word 'parasite' as the reason for excluding viruses; also state that they lack the characteristics of the three domains of life.
